newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end flat on light volume.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end flat on light volume.

text.p: Singapore shares finished flat on Wednesday as investors cautiously mulled over the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to leave short-term interest rate unchanged, dealers said.
"The market is trying to digest what the Fed did last night. It needs reassurance, backed by hard trade figures in Singapore to kick back into action," said a dealer with a foreign house.
"I doubt we will see any respite in the fourth quarter. The Trade and Industry Minister had already forecast an electronics recovery only in early 1997," said a dealer with a local firm.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index rose 4.92 to 2,165.19. Maarket volume was a light 78.59 million shares and gainers led losers by 162 to 130.
There was some light buying of some bank stocks, with DBS foreign and OCBC foreign rising Singapore 40-30 cents.
Creative Technology50 climbed a sharp S$1.45 to S$9.20 on abitrage buying and an upgrading of the stock by Merrill Lynch, dealers said.
Malaysia's Kemayan Corp was suspended when the share price jumped after lunch. It was last traded at S$2.11, up S$0.07 on an active volume of 5.92 million shares.
